scope: One bounded Tailscale-down fault was applied to an already running synthetic Kata job on the existing private Linux host. The root-only driver used the installed Jobs path, installed watchdog socket and service cgroup, and a private copy of the approved synthetic JSON fixture with a guest delay. It did not use OIDC, a browser, or a model call.

initial_idle_probe.limits: This had no active Kata job and did not test delegated execution termination.

active_probe.eventual_run_resolution: failed/null with explicitly unknown execution outcome after root-only inspection

diagnostic_findings: The watchdog's old generic error combines service termination verification and exact-resource cleanup failures. The retained journal reports SIGKILL and the generic error about 0.12 seconds apart, before the service unit completed its stop. This timing suggests a stop-verification race but does not identify the failing substep.

The original 30-second test checks disappearance of container metadata through nerdctl. It does not independently pin the Kata QEMU and shim process identities or establish the host execution termination deadline.
The later failed/null resolution and empty namespace show recovery after the failed observation, not timely cleanup. The execution outcome is unknown.
limits: Do not count this as a passing host-disconnect or 30-second termination check.
The active diagnostic supplied synthetic owner scope directly and did not exercise named-recipient browser authorization or a live model call.
The retained timestamps are observations for this run, not an SLA or proof of absolute safety.
One additional synthetic project/chat/run and audit events remain in the live database; no private project content was used.
privacy: This record contains no cloud project or instance name, account, credential, private URL, run ID, container ID, or transcript.

first_script_attempt.reason: The script expected 17 baseline runs while the live database had 18.

corrected_script_attempt.journal_observation: A containerd journal entry in the same second records a delete cleanup helper for the same container ID. This may explain the group reconstruction observation; exact monitoring evidence is insufficient to establish that explanation.
corrected_script_attempt.whole_group_acceptance_observation: Group reconstruction was observed when the pinned group exited at about 1.212 seconds, and the script immediately returned a failed 30-second whole-group acceptance; no direct whole-group observation was made at t=30 seconds.

resolution_and_recovery.resolver_automatic_cleanup: Ended with CalledProcessError; final service state was not automatically restored.
resolution_and_recovery.manual_resolution: Resolved the exact synthetic run to failed/null with execution outcome unknown.

follow_up: Add candidate identity logging so cleanup helpers and reconstructed groups can be attributed to the exact pinned job group.
Require and verify watchdog socket readiness before invoking the resolver.

documented_containerd_context.summary: The Runtime v2 documentation describes the shim delete subcommand as cleanup when containerd can no longer communicate with a shim, including after a shim is SIGKILLed.
documented_containerd_context.limit: This general documented behavior does not establish why the exact-ID helper was observed in this run and does not classify the separate unknown child.

observation.sampling_limit: The 0.175-second maximum scan gap bounds the observation cadence; it does not prove no transient execution occurred between scans.

untrusted_candidate.identity_observation: A private bounded identity check recorded executable/argv basename nerdctl with 7 arguments.
untrusted_candidate.disposition: Untrusted; do not accept as cleanup or infer that it re-executed the guest.
